Chinese Autonomous Driving Update: XPeng is skipping L3 and betting everything on foundation models to get to L4.

@XPengMotors sees Level 3 as a dead end. The hardware isn't there, the software isn't there, and the regulatory framework definitely isn't there. So they're positioning their second-gen VLA (vision-language-action, a foundation model architecture that maps visual input and language reasoning directly to driving decisions) as the path from L2 straight to L4.

The L3 skip is arguably the most interesting call here. The fundamental problem with L3 is the handoff: the car drives itself until it can't, then the human has to take over instantly. That's arguably more dangerous than just keeping the human in the loop (L2) or removing them entirely (L4). Mercedes is one of the few companies that's actually shipped L3, and the use case is extremely narrow. XPeng is looking at that and saying the juice isn't worth the squeeze.

CEO He Xiaopeng claims internal benchmarks show XPeng roughly 5x ahead of top industry peers on autonomous driving. That's a big number and impossible to verify externally, but the conviction behind it is worth paying attention to.

Gen-2 VLA rolls out to all Ultra and UltraSE models this month. Daily model iterations are reportedly accelerating faster than the team expected.

XPeng merged its intelligent cockpit and autonomous driving units into a single AI center. The goal: treat the car as one cross-domain agent instead of a bunch of separate systems talking to each other.

L4 timeline: He puts full autonomous driving at 1 to 3 years, all vehicles as "active AI agents" at 3 to 5 years. Worth noting that Waymo has been at this for over a decade with deeper pockets and more compute and is still operating in limited geofences. 1 to 3 years is aggressive by anyone's standards.

The real argument underneath all of this is about foundation model scaling. Not incremental ADAS (advanced driver-assistance systems) tuning, not better sensor fusion, but whether you can build a model that generalizes beyond mapped geofences. XPeng's head of general intelligence has been explicit: no foundation model strategy, no L4. Most competitors aren't even framing the problem that way yet.
